title: Panel grooming and probe annotation runway
content:
Summary:
This note defines a compact, repeatable runway for grooming dashboards (panel pruning, role-specific views) and a lightweight probe/trace annotation convention to make investigations faster and reduce noisy panels. The goal: reduce dashboard surface area by ~40% while preserving investigation velocity for oncall and SRE workflows.

Audience:
- Observability engineers (owners of panels/widgets)
- Oncall SREs and operators
- Product/feature owners who care about SLIs

Why we need a runway:
- Many panels have overlapping signals and high query cost.
- Operators spend time switching contexts between dashboards because there is no canonical probe-to-trace mapping.
- Experiment rollouts create transient telemetry that is rarely cleaned up.

High-level approach:
1) Inventory: lightweight scoring of each panel (signal value, cost, owner, frequency of use).
2) Annotate: add probe annotations for critical trace entry points and known failure modes.
3) Prune: retire or archive low-scoring panels into a historical 'panel-archive' dashboard.
4) Gate: add a 90-day auto-expiry tag for non-critical experimental panels.
5) Monitor impact: measure investigation time and query cost post-prune.

Panel scoring rubric (0-10):
- Investigation Value (0-4): how often ops uses this panel to diagnose incidents.
- Fidelity (0-2): is the metric direct or derived? (direct=2, derived=1, fuzzy=0)
- Owner/SLI alignment (0-2): mapped to an SLI or has a clear owner.
- Query cost (0-2): cheaper panels score higher (so cost subtracts: we invert cost to reward cheap panels).

Example: latency-percentile-panel
- Investigation Value: 3
- Fidelity: 2
- Owner alignment: 2
- Query cost: 1
Total = 8 -> keep, but consider consolidation into a composite panel.

Probe / trace annotation convention (lightweight):
We need annotations that travel with traces and can be surfaced on panels. Keep the schema minimal and human-readable. Fields and examples (string fields):
- probe_id: obs.probe.<component>.<short> (e.g., obs.probe.runtime.kv_warmth)
- intent: "investigation" | "slo_anchor" | "cost_anchor" | "experiment"
- owner: team-slug (e.g., eng-serving-runtime)
- severity_hint: low|medium|high (operator guidance for sampling)
- linked_alert: ALERT-123 or empty
- expected_behavior: short sentence (e.g., "kv cache eviction rate < 0.5% per tenant/hour")
- tags: comma-separated short tags

Annotation usage notes:
- Attach probe_id and intent to the root span when request enters Redwood runtime. Secondary spans may copy probe_id for richer session stitching.
- Expected_behavior is optional but very helpful for oncall runbooks.
- severity_hint informs adaptive trace sampling policies (see sampling rules).

Sampling rules (practical):
- Default: 0.5% traces sampled system-wide.
- Probe severity-based override: severity_hint=high -> 20% sample, medium -> 2%, low -> 0.5%.
- SLO breach amplification: if an SLI goes critical, automatically amplify samples for related probes (probe_id matching label) to 50% for 30 minutes.
- Cost control: per-tenant per-hour cap enforced; when cap hit, fall back to event-based sampling (only trace errors and top 1% latency).

Trace retention tiers (cheap, safe defaults):
- Tier A (incident/window): full spans, 30 days (default for high-severity probes and SLO anchors).
- Tier B (ops short-term): aggregated spans + raw headers, 7 days (common operational probes).
- Tier C (bulk sampling): span summaries only, 3 days (low-value / background probes).

Metric naming guidelines (short):
- Use dot-separated component.function.metric (e.g., runtime.kv.cache.evictions.count)
- Suffix with .count, .p50, .p95, .latency_ms, .errors to indicate type
- Include unit in metric metadata, not the metric name (to avoid renames)

Mini metric catalog (to seed the runway):
- runtime.request.latency.p50_ms: p50 request latency measured at runtime ingress
- runtime.request.latency.p95_ms: p95 request latency
- runtime.kv.evictions.count: count of kv cache evictions per minute per node
- serving.tokens.generated.count: tokens produced by serving runtime (useful for cost attribution)
- routing.fallbacks.count: count of requests routed to fallback model variant
- batching.batch_size.avg: average batch size per worker

Dashboard modes (reduce surface area by role):
- Operator mode: compact, investigation-first panels, top of dashboard shows impacted tenants, tail-latency heatmap, and direct links to trace search for selected probes.
- Management mode: high-level SLIs, burn rates, cost per 1k tokens. Low cardinality, lower query frequency.
- Developer mode: feature-level telemetry with experiment tags and request-sample explorer. Not visible by default to operators.

Panel grooming runbook (step-by-step):
1) Weekly triage: owners run 15-min sessions to score 10 panels each using the rubric.
2) For panels scoring <=4: annotate as archival and add expiry tag + reason. Notify owner via Slack @obs-team.
3) Consolidation candidates (score 5-7): merge similar panels into a composite with toggles for quantile views.
4) Keepers (score >=8): ensure probe annotations exist and map to an SLI or incident runbook.
5) Remove or archive: if archived, panel SQL/queries are saved in GCS under obs/panel-archive/<panel_name>.sql and panel replaced with a pointer panel that references the archive.

Change control for dashboards:
- Small changes (<2 panels) can be deployed via dashboard PR with one reviewer from the observability guild.
- Large prune events (>10 panels) require a 48-hour notice and a rollback plan (re-create archived panels within 24 hours if requested).

Investigation play examples (quick wins):
- Slow token path: button to filter traces by probe_id=obs.probe.runtime.kv_warmth + tag tenant_id=heavy-tenant -> show prefix warmness metric and kv.evictions.count in same time window.
- Fallback storm: routing.fallbacks.count correlated with serving.tokens.generated.count and host-level CPU utilization.

Cost vs fidelity heuristics (one-liners):
- Prefer p95 aggregated panels with drilldowns (instead of dozens of distinct percentile panels).
- Replace continuous heavy queries with synthetic probes (sampled runs) if the panel is purely for trend spotting.

Unresolved questions / decisions needed:
- Do we enforce probe_id on all new model-routing spans or only runtime ingress? (decision required by 2026-02-01)
- What SLA do product teams get for archived panel retrieval? (propose 24 hours)
- Exact per-tenant tracing budget and enforcement mechanism: implement as a job or via rate-limiter in ingestion pipeline?

Next steps (owner: eng-observability):
- Pilot (Nov 2025): pick 3 dashboards (serving runtime, routing, KV cache) and score all panels.
- Implement probe annotation library (runtime SDK change) to attach probe_id + severity_hint by Dec 15 2025.
- Update sampling config to honor severity_hint and SLO amplification by Jan 10 2026.
- Run a prune event and measure query-cost delta and median incident investigation time before/after (goal: 30% lower query cost, 15% faster MTTR).

Notes / references:
- Slack: #obs-garden for coordination
- Ticket: JIRA-OBS-2981 (panel grooming pilot)
- Related doc: confluence:OBS/bridge-playbook-789 (instrumentation patterns)

Quick checklist for owners when submitting dashboard PR:
- [ ] Panel score and justification included in PR description
- [ ] probe_id added to traceable spans related to panel metrics
- [ ] Query cost estimate included (bytes scanned / estimated cost)
- [ ] Expiry tag added for experimental panels

End of note.
